newsitem.title: EGYPT: Amoco, Egypt name Citibank as project adviser.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Egypt name Citibank as project adviser.

text.p: Amoco Egypt Oil Company and Egypt's Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) have appointed Citibank as the principal financial adviser for a $1.2 billion liquefied natural gas project, an Amoco statement said on Monday.

Bob Sheppard, President Amoco Egypt, said appointment of the bank was a further step in the development of the project. "Citibank has important experience in the financing of LNG projects," it quoted him as saying.
Amoco Corp of the United States and the Italian oil company Agip are negotiating the details with Turkey.

Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said in April that a pipeline to take natural gas from Egypt to Turkey remained under discussion alongside plans to export Egyptian liquefied natural gas by tanker.

Banbi told a news conference that the liquefaction plant for which a site has been chosen west of Port Said would handle only four billion cubic metres of gas a year, less than half of the 10 billion cubic metres the companies are talking about.
Amoco said it expected to start deliveries in 2001.
When the memorandum of understanding was with the Turkish company Botas in Cairo last November, the parties said the plan was to start exporting in 2000.
